title: 'Hi-De-Ho', 'Willie the Weeper' and how Foots wrote the 'Minnie the Moocher' arrangement
summary: Mills adapted the public-domain 'Willie the Weeper' as 'Minnie the Moocher'; Cab asked Thomas to fix a failed arrangement and he wrote the intro overnight, echoing 'Get Happy'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So that's how the band changed over to Cab Calloway's Orchestra. Because he got big, and he started singing, and after he got "Hi-Di-Ho"... And do you know what "Hi-Di-Ho" came from?

"Hi-Di-Ho" was a public domain song named "Willie The Weeper." And Mills got Parrish to write the words to "Minnie The Moocher"... He took the same lyrics and the same melody, and made it "Minnie The Moocher." That's a story within itself. So we got this arrangement... I wish I could think of that guy's name. He finally went down to Brazil. He was a good arranger, but he didn't fit what needed -- for "Minnie The Moocher" anyway. So we kept fooling with this arrangement, going over it and over it and over it. But it just didn't make... We had enough sense to know it didn't make sense to "Minnie The Moocher."

So we played at the Cotton Club. So Cab said, the night we closed at the Cotton Club to do the recording the next day... He said, "Foots..." He just said, "Do something on 'Minnie The Moocher.'" And that's all he said. So I went home that night, and got up early the next morning, and went to my piano -- and the melody just came to me." And I'll really confess, I copied the tune, the melody a little from "Get Happy." You know, "Get Happy" goes... [SINGS

OPENING 8 BARS] Because Harold Arlen was doing the show at the Cotton Club then. So I got up the next morning, and the melody just came to me... [SINGS REFRAIN] Now, how I constructed it... I hadn't studied harmony. But how I constructed it was a miracle. But the melody just came... [SINGS REFRAIN], then I repeated it... [SINGS REFRAIN] I repeated it again... [SINGS REFRAIN] Then I used the last two bars of "Willie The Weeper"... [SINGS REFRAIN] That's the only thing I didn't write.
